reviewer: AI-assisted geometric observer; not a historical botanical or palaeographic expert
input_exposure: Permitted plant_pairs/label_support and author pair hypotheses, number tables and scan overviews were visible. Label support contains text. This is not complete text blindness. No crossplant lexical hits/results were read and no lexical matching was performed.
coordinate_definition: [x,y,width,height] from top-left of original Yale full image; approximate object-reading regions, normally tens of pixels uncertainty. Whole target drawing boxes may include text.
image_evidence: Whole-image inspection for all 19 canvases: three via full-resolution files and 16 via official 1200-wide overviews; plus official native crops for three source regions. Full-file hashes retained even where observation used the 1200-wide official derivative. No AI redraw or enhancement.
source_locator_clarification: Author overview images are unnumbered photographs; object numbers come from adjacent source number tables, combined with the image row/column. The tables are not independent confirmation of a semantic label.
comparison_unit: Partial illustrated object shape; not historical plant identity, species, sound value or semantic translation.
failure_handling: No pair was omitted. No coarse localization failed after source tables/overviews were checked. Limited identity evidence is retained as limited_or_ambiguous, not discarded. The initial136 canvas deferral was resolved conditionally before inspection, with title conflict preserved.
dependencies: Fragments80,94,95,110 share source physical leaf f99.
Fragments116,133,136 share source physical leaf f100.
Fragments212,213,225,240 share source physical leaf f102, including foldout panels.
Fragment110 has two candidate text loci but one numbered image hypothesis.
Published association of target18v/23r within a bifolio is not an independently checked binding reconstruction here.

limitations: Observer knew the proposed targets and source hypothesis grades; this review is not a blinded forced-choice or specificity experiment.
No unrelated target controls or quantitative shape score were used; a visually plausible partial correspondence does not establish unique identification.
An apparent fit of a label reading would still require independently justified text-to-object attachment and lexical evidence.
Differences in scale, missing portions, folds, paint and preservation limit feature comparison.
No historical plant species identification or archival Petersen-original verification was attempted.
